summary: Large empirical studies show that parallel development creates frequent, partly predictable merge conflicts. Worktrees remove checkout interference but do not reduce semantic overlap or prove conflict-free integration.

items.text: AgenticFlict (2026 preprint) studies more than 29,000 agentic pull requests and reports a 27.67% conflict rate in its dataset, providing direct but very recent evidence that agent parallelism shifts rather than removes integration risk.

Owhadi-Kareshk et al. (2019) analyze 267,657 merge scenarios from 744 repositories and study predictors of merge conflicts; observational repository data supports risk prediction, not a causal worktree benefit.
ConflictBench (Journal of Systems and Software 2024) provides a benchmark for realistic merge-conflict resolution and demonstrates that conflict handling remains a distinct technical task.
A 2020 empirical study of software modularity and merge conflicts identifies structural factors associated with conflicts, supporting ownership and dependency planning alongside workspace isolation.
